referenceSet.title: Double Balloon Detection
referenceSet.description: Visual reference collection teaching Dragonfly's AI to distinguish physically separate speech balloons from logical dialogue units, including cases where multiple balloons contain one continuous sentence or dialogue fragment.
referenceSet.generalInstructions:
# Dragonfly 44 — Double Balloon & Physical Speech Bubble Detection Directive
Target Systems: System #3 (Scanning & Classification) & System #2 (Translation Engine)

## Fundamental Principle: Physical Balloon Boundary != Logical Translation Unit
A physical speech balloon and a logical translation unit represent two fundamentally distinct layers of the manga analysis hierarchy:
1. **Physical Balloon (System #3)**: An independently drawn visual object on the page with its own discrete contour boundary, geometry, and spatial coordinates.
2. **Translation Unit (System #2)**: A logical communicative utterance or sentence that may reference one or multiple physical balloons.

The AI must NEVER collapse, merge, or erase physical balloon boundaries merely because the enclosed text forms a continuous semantic sentence.

### Rule A — Separate Physical Identities (Mandatory)
- Every physically separate speech balloon contour must be detected as an independent `PhysicalBalloon` entity with its own unique `balloonId` and discrete `box_2d` [ymin, xmin, ymax, xmax] (0-1000 scale).
- When two or more balloons are positioned adjacent to one another, stacked vertically, separated by a narrow visual gutter, or touching at an intersecting cusp, they must NEVER be combined into a single unified bounding box.
- Anti-pattern prohibition: Drawing a single bounding box around multiple balloon lobes is strictly prohibited and breaks downstream typesetting, inpainting, and bubble-tail alignment.

### Rule B — Logical Dialogue Association (Multi-Balloon Translation Units)
- Multiple distinct physical balloons belonging to the same continuous utterance must be grouped logically under a single `TranslationUnit` (represented in Dragonfly 44 by `BubbleItem.balloonIds` and `isCombinedDoubleBubble: true`).
- For example:
  * Balloon A (Physical ID: `balloon_top`): "This place is pretty old,"
  * Balloon B (Physical ID: `balloon_bottom`): "after all."
  * Correct Representation:
    - PhysicalBalloon A: independent geometry `[ymin_A, xmin_A, ymax_A, xmax_A]`
    - PhysicalBalloon B: independent geometry `[ymin_B, xmin_B, ymax_B, xmax_B]`
    - TranslationUnit: references ["balloon_top", "balloon_bottom"], subBoxes: [box_A, box_B], combined text: "This place is pretty old, after all."
- Preserving physical sub-boxes guarantees that the typesetter can distribute translated text proportionally across both lobes without overflow.

### Rule C — Narrow Balloons & Multi-Line Wrapping vs. Separate Balloons
- Distinguish between multi-line text wrapping inside ONE narrow balloon and dialogue distributed across SEPARATE physical balloons.
- A single physical balloon contour containing broken or wrapped lines (e.g. "L-LEO?!\nWHY WOULD YOU--?!") remains ONE `PhysicalBalloon`. Do not fragment a single contour into multiple objects.
- Physical contour boundaries—not line breaks—determine physical balloon identity.

### Rule D — Typography & TypeR Symbol Conventions
- Maintain Dragonfly 44's authoritative TypeR classifications:
  * Standard spoken dialogue: `dialogue` / `speech_bubbles` (prefix: "":)
  * Internal thoughts: `thought` / `thought_bubbles` (prefix: ():)
  * Shouting/screaming: `shouting` / `scream` (prefix: %:)
  * Stepped narrative captions: `narration` / `box` (prefix: [ ]:)
  * Floating in-art text / SFX: `sfx` / `outside_text` (prefix: OT:)
- Maintain Arabic RTL requirements: symbol placement and reading direction must conform to project specifications without glyph corruption.

### Rule E — Geometry & Shape Integrity
- Bounding boxes must tightly envelop the actual physical balloon contour.
- Do not encompass surrounding background art or adjacent unrelated characters.
- Retain micro-bubbles and trailing whispers (e.g. tiny `...doomed` bubbles in multi-bubble chains); never prune them as noise.

### Rule F — Speaker Attribution & Panel-First Reading Order
- Follow Dragonfly 44's panel-first reading order: resolve panel sequence first (RTL: top-right to bottom-left), then sequence intra-panel speech balloons.
- Overlapping speech balloons from DIFFERENT speakers (e.g. rapid conversational interruptions) must NOT be grouped into a single TranslationUnit. They represent separate speakers and must yield distinct TranslationUnits.

examples.title: Horizontal Double-Balloon Pair with Cusp Intersection
examples.aiNote: Image #01 demonstrates the canonical manga double-balloon arrangement with an intersecting cusp. In both the top panel ("All right, that's fixed!" + "Next up, the door!") and bottom panel ("But if you do want to keep it going..." + "marry a man you can trust to take care of Yadorigi"), two distinct balloon lobes merge at a physical cusp. Detect two separate PhysicalBalloon objects per pair. Associate both with a single TranslationUnit in Japanese RTL reading sequence (Right lobe first, Left lobe second). Never draw a single bounding box enclosing both lobes.
examples.expectedBehaviour: Detect 4 discrete PhysicalBalloon entities (2 per panel). Group top pair into TU_1 with reading order [Right=1, Left=2]. Group bottom pair into TU_2 with reading order [Right=1, Left=2]. Preserve subBoxes for both physical lobes.

examples.title: Multi-Element Balloon Chain with Micro-Bubble & Multi-Speaker Separation
examples.aiNote: Image #02 demonstrates two critical challenges: a 3-element descending balloon chain including a tiny micro-bubble ("...doomed"), and multiple conversational speakers in the same panel. Detect the white-haired girl's 3-element chain as three independent PhysicalBalloon objects linked to one TranslationUnit, specifically preserving the micro-bubble rather than pruning it. Simultaneously, maintain absolute physical and logical separation from the black-haired girl ("We somehow made it through...") and brown-haired girl ("That's so true~").
examples.expectedBehaviour: Detect all physical balloons independently. White-haired girl's main bubble and attached micro-bubble ("...doomed") must be linked under TU_2 without merging geometries. Separate speakers into independent TranslationUnits.

examples.title: Stepped Rectangular Narration Boxes (Multi-Box Exposition)
examples.aiNote: Image #03 demonstrates that multi-box units occur frequently with rectangular narration boxes (TypeR tag: [ ]: / box) as well as curved speech bubbles. In both panels, rectangular narrative boxes overlap in a stepped diagonal cascade to form continuous exposition. Detect each rectangular box as a distinct PhysicalBalloon (primaryClass: "narration"). Group the overlapping stepped boxes into a single TranslationUnit. Do not merge the stepped boxes into one bounding polygon or rectangle.
examples.expectedBehaviour: Detect 2 stepped narration boxes in top panel and 2 in bottom panel. Assign primaryClass="narration" and Typer prefix="[ ]:". Maintain separate physical geometries while associating each stepped pair to one TranslationUnit.

examples.title: Full-Page Layout & Panel-First Hierarchy for Multi-Box Chains
examples.aiNote: Image #04 demonstrates full-page layout integration and strict adherence to the panel-first reading order. Three successive panels each feature a stepped pair of rectangular narration boxes. The AI must enforce panel isolation first: never group Box 2 of Panel 1 with Box 1 of Panel 2 across panel boundaries. Intra-panel stepped boxes must be sequenced and combined locally before evaluating page-level reading flow.
examples.expectedBehaviour: Perform panel segmentation first. Group stepped boxes strictly within their owning panel (Panel 1: TU_1, Panel 2: TU_2, Panel 3: TU_3). Enforce Manga RTL page reading order: Panel 1 (top-right) -> Panel 2 (top-left) -> Panel 3 (bottom).

examples.title: Morphological Variety: Vertical Stacks, Staggered Ovals & Jagged Shout Balloons
examples.aiNote: Image #05 demonstrates that double-balloon boundary separation applies across all morphological varieties. This includes vertical smooth stacks (top-right), diagonal staggered pairs (stairs and bottom-left), and jagged burst/shout balloons ("S-" + "SHUT UP!"). Spiky contour lines must not cause polygon extraction errors or accidental merging into a single convex hull. Retain separate PhysicalBalloon boundaries and assign TypeR shouting prefix (%:) to burst pairs.
examples.expectedBehaviour: Detect spiky double balloons ("S-" + "SHUT UP!") as 2 discrete PhysicalBalloons with shouting (%:) classification grouped under TU_5. Detect smooth vertical and staggered double pairs with independent boxes.

examples.title: Speech Balloons vs. In-Art Directional Text & Status Labels
examples.aiNote: Image #06 demonstrates the crucial boundary between character speech balloons and in-art floating directional annotations. In the middle panel, the characters have floating status text with downward arrows ("Food ↓", "Costs ↓") alongside standard speech ("Our food expenses are completely wrecking the household budget, you know!"). The floating directional labels must be classified as independent in-art text (TypeR: OT: / outside_text) and NEVER swallowed or merged into the character's speech balloon TranslationUnit.
examples.expectedBehaviour: Isolate "Food ↓" and "Costs ↓" as independent text regions (primaryClass: "sfx", Typer prefix: "OT:"). Do not attach them to character dialogue balloons or merge their bounding boxes.

examples.title: Authoritative Negative Reference: Merged Single-Box Anti-Pattern
examples.aiNote: Image #07 serves as Dragonfly 44's explicit negative ground-truth example (Counter-example / Anti-pattern). Hand-annotated with red boxes crossed out with red X marks and the explicit directive: "rwong way to do dobble bubbles is to make them a single bubble and translate the full sentes at ones, avoide falling for this". Merging physically separate speech balloon lobes into a single bounding box to "translate the full sentence at once" is an absolute system failure. The AI must reject combined bounding boxes, detect discrete physical boundaries for each lobe, and link them via logical translation units.
examples.expectedBehaviour: Identify all crossed-out single bounding boxes as erroneous anti-patterns. Reject unified boxes covering multiple lobes. Output discrete physical geometries for each lobe with shared TranslationUnit references.

examples.title: Multi-Speaker Overlap & Single-Balloon Multi-Line Text Wrapping
examples.aiNote: Image #08 demonstrates two essential disambiguation rules: 1) Multi-speaker overlap: in the top panel, two balloons overlap physically ("UH, I DON'T THINK--" vs. "OKAY. YOU'RE ON.") but belong to DIFFERENT speakers. Physical overlap does NOT imply shared TranslationUnit; each speaker must receive an independent TranslationUnit. 2) Single-balloon multi-line wrapping (Rule C): in the bottom panel, a single physical contour contains "L-LEO?!" and "WHY WOULD YOU--?!" (indicated by the orange arrow). Wrapped or multi-line text within ONE continuous physical contour remains ONE PhysicalBalloon. Do not fragment a single balloon into multiple objects.
examples.expectedBehaviour: Top panel: Detect two overlapping PhysicalBalloons, assign to separate TranslationUnits (TU_1 and TU_2) due to different speakers. Bottom panel: Detect exactly ONE PhysicalBalloon enclosing both lines of text ("L-LEO?!" and "WHY WOULD YOU--?!").
